references.text: Moses and Aaron gather the elders of Israel and tell them what the Lord has said, as a direct fulfillment of the command in 3:16.
Joseph uses the same expression 'פָּקֹד פָּקַדְתִּי' (I have surely visited you) and promises that God will lead the Israelites out of Egypt.
God reveals himself as the God of Abraham, using the same formulation 'אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם' found here.
God presents himself to Jacob as 'the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac,' the same ancestral formula used in this verse.
Earlier in the same chapter, God introduces himself as 'your father's God, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.'
Reference to Joseph's prophecy that God would 'visit' (פָּקֹד יִפְקֹד) the Israelites, using the same verb root as in 3:16.
Jesus quotes this formulation 'the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob' when he speaks about the resurrection of the dead.
Stephen quotes this verse in his speech and refers to 'the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.'
Peter uses the expression 'the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of our fathers' in his speech at the temple.
God's promise to Abraham that his descendants would be strangers in a land and then be delivered, which is now fulfilled.
The identical title 'God of the Fathers' links God's revelation in the burning bush with the requirement that this must be the foundation of the people's faith.
Connects God's intervention to free from Egypt directly to the fulfillment of the promise of the land given to the fathers.
Ezekiel summarizes and confirms the theology from Exodus 3:16 by calling it the moment when God made himself known in Egypt.
Refers directly to the same historical event (the exodus from Egypt) as planned and carried out by God.
Links God's plan to see the suffering in Egypt (Exodus 3) with the historical experience of deliverance (Deuteronomy).
